summary: Milestone 2026.10.705 completed 12 experiments (3 compute-bound, 9 synthesis-only) across 127.9 total wall-time minutes (averaging 11 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was led by synthesis task 'Measure complete atomic batch transactions through Python and Rust' (58.31 minutes), followed by compute-bound tasks 'Measure current Qwen acquisition plus matched durable service branches' (32.7 minutes), 'Capture bounded Qwen evidence on fixed fit and tune sources' (13.89 minutes), and 'Seal reserved Qwen evidence and frozen predictions' (9.21 minutes), and synthesis task 'Bound durable workload acceleration and preserve each board obligation' (5.13 minutes). Point-in-time GPU monitor polling observed 0% utilization across both NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs with 4MB memory allocated outside active runs, and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is recorded as false as no compute-bound idle anomalies or multi-model parallel dispatch requirements were present.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis task 'Measure complete atomic batch transactions through Python and Rust' consumed 58.31 of the 127.9 total milestone wall-time minutes (45.6%), representing the single largest latency concentration.

Compute-bound execution consumed 55.80 minutes (43.6% of milestone wall time) across three single-model tasks without intra-task stage breakdown: 'Measure current Qwen acquisition plus matched durable service branches' (32.7 minutes), 'Capture bounded Qwen evidence on fixed fit and tune sources' (13.89 minutes), and 'Seal reserved Qwen evidence and frozen predictions' (9.21 minutes).

The top two slowest tasks ('Measure complete atomic batch transactions through Python and Rust' and 'Measure current Qwen acquisition plus matched durable service branches') combined for 91.01 minutes (71.2% of milestone wall time).

Milestone timing relied on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction due to zero commits found on the live git-log path, leaving intra-task phases (batch transaction processing, Qwen acquisition, fitting/tuning, and receipt serialization) uninstrumented without granular telemetry.

Static GPU monitor polling provides only point-in-time snapshots (0% utilization, 4MB allocated across both RTX 3090 GPUs) rather than continuous execution-window telemetry during active compute-bound runs.
improvements_suggested: Profile and optimize the cross-language atomic batch transaction pipeline in 'Measure complete atomic batch transactions through Python and Rust' (58.31 minutes) to reduce serialization and evaluation overhead.
Instrument experiment runners with granular intra-task sub-phase timers to isolate latency across model acquisition, durable service branching, inference passes, and receipt serialization.
Emit synchronous start and finish lifecycle timestamps directly into task result receipts during conductor execution to eliminate reliance on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction.
Deploy continuous in-flight accelerator telemetry sampling during compute-bound execution windows to dynamically measure GPU utilization and memory bandwidth.
Enforce DualGPURunner orchestration strictly for concurrent workloads executing two or more distinct models in parallel, avoiding misapplication to single-model Qwen tasks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Profile and optimize the cross-language atomic batch transaction processing pipeline in 'Measure complete atomic batch transactions through Python and Rust' (which accounted for 58.31 minutes of milestone wall time).
Instrument experiment runners with granular intra-task sub-phase timers to isolate model acquisition, durable service branching, inference, and artifact serialization latency.
Persist structured start and finish lifecycle timestamps directly into experiment receipt artifacts to replace disk-mtime fallback reconstruction.
meta_reflection: Milestone 2026.10.705 completed 12 experiments (3 compute-bound, 9 synthesis-only) in 127.9 wall-time minutes, dominated by cross-language atomic batch transactions (58.31 minutes) and Qwen service acquisition (32.7 minutes). Point-in-time GPU monitor polling observed 0% utilization across both RTX 3090 GPUs with 4MB allocated outside active runs, and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false as the compute-bound tasks did not involve multi-model parallel execution. Highest-leverage operational gains lie in profiling atomic batch transaction latency and instrumenting granular intra-task phase timers, with estimated time savings set to 0% pending empirical phase telemetry.
